title: cicd-rollback-breadcrumbs
content:
Purpose / context:
- Personal debugging scratchpad for the canary rollback during 2025-11-10 release (RELEASE-4212).
- Notes, commands tried, short error excerpts, and hypotheses for follow-ups.

Quick summary of event:
- Deployment: service-api (k8s, helm) rolled as canary -> increased 5xxs for external /v1/predict endpoint from ~0.2% to ~6% within 10m.
- Canary traffic: 10% via router rule (traffic-split).
- Time window: 2025-11-10T14:12Z deploy started; by 14:22Z alert fired.
- Action: paused rollout and rolled back canary image to previous stable tag. Need to capture exact commands and outputs below.

Observed metrics / logs (short):
- Grafana: canary pod error-rate spike chart shows 5xx up to 6.3% at 14:20Z.
- Sentry snippets: 2025-11-10T14:18Z
  TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'tokenize')
  at Tokenizer.tokenize (/srv/service-api/src/tokenizer.js:82:23)
  requestId: 8f6a2b9c
  stack: ...tokenizer.js:82
- K8s pod logs (canary pod service-api-78c4f7d9b6-ptx2):
  2025-11-10T14:17:41Z ERROR [request] id=8f6a2b9c status=500 body="TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined"
  2025-11-10T14:17:45Z WARN [startup] model load took 28.4s (expected < 8s)

Initial hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: Model artifact mismatch / new artifact missing expected metadata -> tokenizer fails for some requests.
- Hypothesis B: Cold-start/pathological startup due to missing cache warmers -> first few requests hit slow code paths and throw transient errors.
- Hypothesis C: Config drift: env var FEATURE_TOKENIZER_V2 enabled in canary but not in stable; codepath assumes new tokenizer available.
- Hypothesis D: Container image built with different node dependency (transitive) (package-lock/regeneration) causing runtime mismatch.

Commands tried (chronological) and outputs (captured):
1) Inspect deployment status (helm + kubectl):
- helm list --namespace prod | grep service-api
  -> release service-api  1.23.4-canary-20251110  deployed
- kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=service-api -o wide\  
  -> pods: service-api-78c4f7d9b6-ptx2 (canary), service-api-5b7d9c7f8c-qm2l (stable)

2) Tail pod logs (canary):
- kubectl -n prod logs -f service-api-78c4f7d9b6-ptx2 --tail=200
  -> see repeated TypeError and model load warning.

3) Check image tags to correlate artifact versions:
- kubectl -n prod describe pod service-api-78c4f7d9b6-ptx2 | grep Image
  -> Image: registry.redwood.com/service-api:2025.11.10-canary-rc3
- kubectl -n prod describe pod service-api-5b7d9c7f8c-qm2l | grep Image
  -> Image: registry.redwood.com/service-api:2025.10.29-stable-45

4) Validate container filesystem for metadata file expected by tokenizer (quick exec):
- kubectl -n prod exec -it service-api-78c4f7d9b6-ptx2 -- ls -l /srv/models/metadata.json
  -> ls: /srv/models/metadata.json: No such file or directory
- kubectl -n prod exec -it service-api-5b7d9c7f8c-qm2l -- cat /srv/models/metadata.json
  -> {"tokenizer": "v1", "model_sha": "abc123"}

5) Inspect image layers locally (artifact registry) for canary tag (quick):
- crane manifest registry.redwood.com/service-api:2025.11.10-canary-rc3 | jq .
  -> shows new layer packaging but metadata.json absent in /srv/models. Suspect build step missed copying metadata.

Actions taken (immediate):
- Paused canary traffic routing at 14:25Z: updated traffic-split to 0% canary. (router CLI)
- Triggered rollback: helm rollback service-api 1 --namespace prod
  -> helm rollback service-api 1
  Output: Rollback to revision 1 succeeded
- Confirmed pods returned to stable image: kubectl -n prod get pods (stable pods ready).

Rollback verification checks run:
- Smoke: /health returns 200 for stable pods.
- Canary-specific tests: N/A after rollback.
- Post-rollback alert: no further 5xx spikes.

Root cause (working hypothesis after quick triage):
- Build pipeline (release-job) omitted copying /srv/models/metadata.json into final image for canary tag 2025.11.10-canary-rc3. New tokenizer code assumes metadata presence, causing runtime TypeError.
- Why only canary? Canary was built from PR that updated Dockerfile (accidentally changed WORKDIR or multistage copy order).

Repro steps locally (to validate hypothesis):
- Pull canary image: docker pull registry.redwood.com/service-api:2025.11.10-canary-rc3
- docker run --rm -it registry.redwood.com/service-api:2025.11.10-canary-rc3 sh -c "ls -l /srv/models || true"
  -> confirmed metadata.json missing.

Next steps / TODOs (owners):
- (Aisha) Open PR to fix Dockerfile multistage copy and add unit to CI that checks for /srv/models/metadata.json presence in built image. Blocker: patch must include test and pipeline change. Target: hotfix build and redeploy.
- (Matt) Create a release fix image tag 2025.11.10-hotfix1 and push to registry; run internal canary with additional health checks (traffic at 2% initially).
- (Diego) Add pipeline assertion to release job (makefile target or minimal test in CI) to validate model metadata exists.
- (ENG-Infra) Add an automated image content linter to CI images with a white-list of required paths.

Diagnostics notes / lessons learned:
- Need stronger pre-deploy invariant checks for artifacts that runtime depends on (metadata, model files).
- Canary traffic split need ability to instantly kill canary (we had to patch router rule via CLI; automate rollback trigger on error-rate thresholds).
- Add a simple smoke test that runs inside the image (container-level) to detect missing files.

Past related tickets / references:
- RELEASE-4020: previous canary where model path mistmatch surfaced (Feb 2025) - similar root cause.
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/service-api/pull/1284 (contains the code changes that introduced new tokenizer).

Short-term safe checklist for re-release:
1) Fix Dockerfile (copy metadata).
2) Build hotfix image with CI assertion passing.
3) Deploy to staging and run full smoke + long-tail load test.
4) Deploy to prod canary at 2% with extended health-window (15m) and auto-kill on >1% 5xx.
5) If stable after 30m increase to 10% then full.

Notes to self (random debugging breadcrumbs):
- Look at job 'release-job:build-image' in GitHub Actions workflow -> artifact packaging step uses tar and then COPY -- from=builder /app/dist -> maybe metadata created under different path.
- npm ci vs npm install difference might have caused packaging script to skip copying metadata script.
- Remember to update Confluence runbook for rollbacks with exact helm revision numbers and router CLI commands.

End of notes.

Recorded by: Aisha Khan (release-engineering)
